note: India: Nepalese nationals may cross the open border without passport or visa and live and work in India (the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship). Others come on the Employment Visa, which the Ministry of Home Affairs' FAQs name for foreign artists engaged to perform for the length of a contract, granted by a mission for up to a year and extendable to five, with registration at the FRRO within two weeks; Indian missions send short paid performances to the business visa, not modelled apart. Bhutan's nationals aren't modelled separately. Read from a reproduction of the MHA FAQs and from Wikipedia, since the Bureau of Immigration's, the MHA's and the missions' pages refuse this client.

sources.title: TaxGuru, Business Visa, Employment Visa and the MHA's Frequently Asked Questions
sources.said: Foreign artists engaged to conduct regular performances for the duration of the employment contract given by Hotels, Clubs, other organizations. ... A foreign national coming to India for employment may initially be granted an Employment Visa by the Indian Missions abroad upto one year.

sources.title: Wikipedia, India–Nepal relations
sources.said: The Indo-Nepal border is open; Nepalese and Indian nationals may move freely across the border without passports or visas and may live and work in either country.
